title: Are There Michelin Star Restaurants in Sydney or Melbourne?
description: No Sydney or Melbourne restaurant has a Michelin star. Australia’s first 11, revealed on 14 October 2026, are all in South Australia. What they cost.
h1: Are There Michelin Star Restaurants in Sydney, Melbourne or Anywhere in Australia?
summary: Australia’s first 11 Michelin-starred restaurants, revealed on 14 October 2026, are all in South Australia. What they cost, and why Sydney and Melbourne have none.
figure: 11 starred restaurants, all in South Australia
keywords: are there any michelin star restaurants in australia
does australia have michelin star restaurants
body:
Yes, but not in Sydney or Melbourne. Australia won its first Michelin stars on 14 October 2026, but the MICHELIN Guide covers only South Australia, so all 11 starred restaurants are there: Magill Estate Restaurant in Adelaide with two stars and ten with one, from the city to the Barossa and the Clare Valley.

For years the answer to “are there any Michelin star restaurants in Australia?” was no, because Michelin had never published a guide here. Here are Australia’s first starred restaurants and what a meal at each costs, why Sydney and Melbourne still have none, when they might, and how chef’s hats compare with stars.

Australia’s first Michelin stars: South Australia, 14 October 2026

The first MICHELIN Guide South Australia, which Michelin calls the 2027 edition, was revealed at the Adelaide Convention Centre on 14 October 2026. It came from a partnership with the state government announced in May, when Michelin’s International Director, Gwendal Poullennec, pointed to the state’s “impressive diversity of culinary expressions within a single destination”. Of the 77 restaurants in the guide, 11 have Michelin stars, 16 a Bib Gourmand for good cooking at moderate prices, and 50 are listed as MICHELIN Selected. There is still no MICHELIN Guide Australia covering the whole country: this one is for South Australia alone.

The only two-star restaurant is Magill Estate Restaurant, Penfolds’ dining room above its original vineyard in the Adelaide foothills, where chef Scott Huggins’s tasting experience costs {{dinner:magill-estate-restaurant}} per person and a shorter Signature Menu A$295. The other four in and around the city have one star: Restaurant Botanic, in a rotunda in the Botanic Garden ({{dinner:restaurant-botanic}}), Aurora at ILA on Light Square ({{dinner:aurora-at-ila}}), Esmay in a restored Hackney pub ({{dinner:esmay}}) and arkhé, cooking over fire in Norwood (from {{dinner:arkhe}}). All five, with their lunch and wine pairing prices, are on our Adelaide Michelin star restaurants page.

The other six are in the Adelaide Hills and the wine regions, and three open only at lunch. In the Hills, Aptos in Stirling serves 16 courses in a former church for {{dinner:aptos}}, and LVN Restaurant at Bird in Hand in Woodside a lunch menu for {{lunch:lvn-bird-in-hand}}. Hentley Farm in the Barossa charges {{lunch:hentley-farm}} for its Discovery menu at lunch, Maxwell Restaurant in McLaren Vale {{dinner:maxwell-restaurant}}, and Anvers at Kangarilla {{lunch:anvers}}. The cheapest way into a Michelin-starred dining room in Australia is the two-course lunch at Skillogalee Barrel House in the Clare Valley, at {{lunch:skillogalee-barrel-house}}. Every one is on our South Australia page, and our Australia page will grow as other states join the guide.

Why Australia had no Michelin stars until 2026

Michelin only awards stars where it publishes a guide, and until 2026 it had never published one for Australia. New guides are expensive to launch, and these days most arrive through a partnership with a tourism body that helps pay for the inspections. Australia’s restaurants were rated by home-grown guides instead, above all the Good Food Guide’s chef’s hats.

Are there any Michelin star restaurants in Sydney?

No. No Sydney restaurant has ever held a Michelin star, and none could win one on 14 October 2026: the first guide covers South Australia only, and Michelin hasn’t announced a guide for New South Wales. Sydney’s top restaurants are rated with hats in the Good Food Guide instead, and two of its four three-hat restaurants in the 2026 edition have since closed. Quay, Peter Gilmore’s restaurant overlooking the Opera House, served its last dinner on 14 February 2026 after 23 consecutive years with three hats. Oncore by Clare Smyth at Crown Sydney, the Australian sister of her three-star CORE in London, closed on 28 February.

That leaves Saint Peter, Josh Niland’s fish restaurant in Paddington, and Sixpenny in Stanmore as the city’s three-hat restaurants. For a meal at Clare Smyth’s level now, the nearest is CORE itself in Notting Hill, where dinner costs £275 (about $365) per person (see London’s prices).

Are there any Michelin star restaurants in Melbourne?

No, for the same reason: no Melbourne restaurant has held a star, and Victoria isn’t part of the first guide. Melbourne’s highest honours are three hats in The Age Good Food Guide, which in 2026 went to Vue de monde, Amaru and Minamishima in the city, and Brae, Dan Hunter’s farm restaurant at Birregurra in the Otways.

When could Sydney and Melbourne get Michelin stars?

Michelin hasn’t said. New guides usually follow a deal with a tourism body, as South Australia’s did, so stars for Sydney or Melbourne would most likely start with New South Wales or Victoria signing one. Michelin already rates hotels in both cities, though: its 2026 Michelin Keys, announced in September, went to 54 Australian hotels, among them Capella Sydney with two Keys and The Langham in both Sydney and Melbourne with one. Keys rate where you stay, not where you eat.

For now, the nearest Michelin-starred restaurants to both cities are in South Australia. Adelaide is about 650 km from Melbourne, an hour and a quarter by air, and 1,160 km from Sydney, about two hours, and several of its starred tables are an hour’s drive from the airport in the Hills and the wine regions. Across the Tasman, New Zealand’s 15 starred restaurants, from its first guide in June 2026, are about three hours from Sydney.

Chef’s hats vs Michelin stars

Hats are Australia’s answer to stars, awarded each year by the Good Food Guide published with The Sydney Morning Herald and The Age, on a scale of one to three. The two systems aren’t equivalent. Hats come from the guide’s scored reviews, while Michelin’s inspectors are anonymous, pay for their meals and judge only the food on the plate. Far more restaurants hold a hat than hold stars in any comparable Michelin city, so a hat isn’t a star in waiting, though the three-hat restaurants are the ones most often tipped for stars. South Australia’s first selection bore that out only in part: inspectors starred country kitchens as readily as the state’s best-known dining rooms, and more than half the one-star restaurants are outside Adelaide.

faq.q: Does Australia have Michelin star restaurants?
faq.a: Yes, since 14 October 2026, when the first MICHELIN Guide South Australia gave stars to 11 restaurants: Magill Estate Restaurant in Adelaide with two and ten with one. All are in South Australia, the only state the guide covers.

faq.q: Why doesn’t Sydney have a Michelin star restaurant?
faq.a: Michelin only awards stars where it publishes a guide, and its only Australian guide covers South Australia. New guides usually start through a partnership with a tourism body, so Sydney would need New South Wales to sign one.

faq.q: Which Australian restaurant has two Michelin stars?
faq.a: Magill Estate Restaurant, Penfolds’ restaurant at Magill in Adelaide’s eastern foothills, led by chef Scott Huggins. No Australian restaurant has three stars.
